_meta.indication: Treatment of adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older who weigh at least 40 kg with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis whose disease is not adequately controlled with topical prescription therapies or when those therapies are not advisable; can be used with or without topical corticosteroids.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group monotherapy study with a 16-week induction and 36-week maintenance period
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and adolescent (≥12 to <18 years and weigh at least 40kg) patients with moderate-to-severe AD
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percentage of subjects with an IGA score of 0 or 1 and a ≥2-point reduction from Baseline at Week 16
pivotal_trials.n: 424 enrolled; primary efficacy analysis included 283 EBGLYSS and 141 placebo
pivotal_trials.result: IGA 0 or 1 at Week 16: 43% EBGLYSS vs 13% placebo (difference 30%, 95% CI 22%, 38%); EASI-75: 59% vs 16%

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group monotherapy study with a 16-week induction and 36-week maintenance period
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and adolescent (≥12 to <18 years and weigh at least 40kg) patients with moderate-to-severe AD
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percentage of subjects with an IGA score of 0 or 1 and a ≥2-point reduction from Baseline at Week 16 (same as Study KGAB)
pivotal_trials.n: 445 enrolled; primary efficacy analysis included 281 EBGLYSS and 146 placebo
pivotal_trials.result: IGA 0 or 1 at Week 16: 33% EBGLYSS vs 11% placebo (difference 22%, 95% CI 14%, 30%); EASI-75: 52% vs 18%

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study of lebrikizumab in combination with topical corticosteroids (TCS) over a 16-week treatment period
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and adolescent (≥12 to <18 years and weigh at least 40kg) patients with moderate-to-severe AD
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percentage of subjects with an IGA score of 0 or 1 and a ≥2-point reduction from Baseline at Week 16 (same as Studies KGAB and KGAC)
pivotal_trials.result: IGA 0 or 1 at Week 16: 41% EBGLYSS+TCS vs 22% placebo+TCS; EASI-75: 70% vs 42%

key_safety: Most common (≥1%) adverse reactions are conjunctivitis (10% EBGLYSS monotherapy vs 3% placebo), injection site reactions (3% vs 1%), and herpes zoster (<1%). Discontinuations due to AEs were 2.4% (EBGLYSS) vs 1.8% (placebo) in monotherapy trials.
target_moa: Lebrikizumab is an IgG4 monoclonal antibody that binds to IL-13 and selectively inhibits IL-13 signaling through the IL-4 receptor alpha/IL-13 receptor alpha-1 pathway, blocking the downstream effects of IL-13, a cytokine involved in Type 2 inflammation.

rems.type: No risk evaluation and mitigation strategy are warranted.

requirement.text: 4514-3 Conduct or participate in a relevant Pregnancy Exposure Registry, a prospective registry based observational exposure cohort study that compares the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to lebrikizumab during pregnancy to an unexposed control population.

citations.quote: 4514-3 Conduct or participate in a relevant Pregnancy Exposure Registry, a prospective registry based observational exposure cohort study that compares the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to lebrikizumab during pregnancy to an unexposed control population. The registry should be designed to detect and record major and minor congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, elective terminations, small for gestational age, preterm birth, and any other adverse pregnancy outcomes. These outcomes will be assessed throughout pregnancy. Infant outcomes, including effects on postnatal growth and development, neonatal deaths, and serious infections, will be assessed through at least the first year of life.

requirement.text: 4514-4 Conduct an additional pregnancy study that uses a different design from the Pregnancy Exposure Registry (for example a retrospective cohort study using claims or electronic medical record data with outcome validation or a case control study) to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, and small for gestational age and preterm birth in women exposed to lebrikizumab during pregnancy compared to an unexposed control population.
